findings.title: Money and account endpoints do not bind the caller to the resource
findings.explanation: CORS and JSON parsing are the only source middleware. Direct assets:4003 accepts buyer_id/seller_id/user_id and arbitrary funding amounts without an authenticated actor. A holding-existence check does not authorize the requester. Funding has no provider-confirmed source or durable duplicate protection. Gateway routes do not expose all these mutations, but direct service endpoints do.

findings.title: Settlement does not preserve amount and per-currency invariants
findings.explanation: Negative quantities/amounts pass local checks. Wallet UPDATE selects user_id only and can debit/credit multiple currencies, while the journal names one first wallet. Locked funds/status/currency are ignored; price uses binary Number; no durable request idempotency. Database transactions and row locks are useful, but insufficient. Isolated source probes prove control-flow acceptance, not any unseen database constraints.

findings.title: Asset reads and writes use independent databases and incompatible schemas
findings.explanation: GET assets/profile uses SQLite seeded name/kitchen/base_value rows. POST assets writes PostgreSQL food_id/asset_code/current_value through assetCreationService. No synchronization exists; newly created assets need not appear in listings. POST assets multi-write service also lacks a shared DB transaction; /economy/create has one but remains a separate path.

findings.title: Forty-one inline route registrations are inside a catch handler
findings.explanation: Of88 inline GET/POST declarations,47 register at startup. The other41 register only after memory recall rejects, and can register again on each error. Mounted modular routers may cover some overlapping URLs; this is a declaration count, not41 guaranteed unique inaccessible URLs. Real HTTP /brain/feedback/1 returned404 at boot.

findings.title: Verification handlers fail and verification records are invented
findings.explanation: Server imports verificationEngine but /verify handlers call undefined verification: GET verified500 in HTTP, POST reproduced ReferenceError. Actual verifyFood returns VERIFIED with random confidence and null evidence. GET asset-profile invokes it and creates a record, so reading a profile changes claimed verification history.

findings.title: Root npm installation lifecycle invokes itself
findings.explanation: install script is npm install. Ordinary npm install or ci runs the root lifecycle, which invokes another installation and lifecycle. Definition inspected; recursive lifecycle deliberately not executed. Dependencies were installed with --ignore-scripts and an offline cached ci before the build.

findings.title: Gateway does not expose the newer brain and wallet portfolio APIs
findings.explanation: /api/brain proxies to intelligence4005 while newer routes live on assets4003; /api/wallet proxies to wallet4002 while portfolio/intelligence live on assets4003. Observed /api/brain/agent/runs/example upstream404 on4005. Active frontend mostly bypasses gateway using localhost URLs.

findings.title: PostgreSQL setup and notification startup are incomplete
findings.explanation: No canonical complete PostgreSQL bootstrap, migrations or environment example is tracked; scripts assume an existing Docker DB/schema and author-specific home path. PG* and POSTGRES_* configuration families diverge. Notification has no manifest, workspace/all-service startup or CORS middleware. A clean checkout cannot reproduce the full financial/intelligence system from README alone.

findings.title: Three navigation destinations and exchange pickers reference missing variables
findings.explanation: liveAssets exists only inside WalletScreen. IntelligenceScreen and KitchenDetailScreen reference it outside that scope; tradeAssets is never declared. Intelligence/Kitchens tabs, kitchen detail and opening an exchange picker throw ReferenceError. There is no error boundary. Focused Node evaluation reproduced each missing-name failure; no browser test was performed by this reviewer.

findings.title: Wallet always displays fallback balances instead of fetched balances
findings.explanation: Hook returns wallet={cash,food}; UI searches wallet.wallets. All three reads miss: brief shows 0 ə, cash shows 0 in selected label currency and schwa card shows 42 ə, irrespective of database balances. Node probe mapped real-shaped sample EUR 125/ə88 and reproduced displayed 0/42.

findings.title: Exchange success is a local demonstration, not a completed trade
findings.explanation: Confirm only appends an in-memory item and sets step=done. It never calls the available executeTrade endpoint, changes holdings, updates balances or persists state. Reload/unmount loses the exchange. UI says Exchange complete without executing a backend effect.

findings.title: Market misses assets that arrive after its first render
findings.explanation: Memo calculation captures marketAssets but dependencies include category/query only. If user opens market before asset fetch resolves, filtered remains [] on context update; changing a filter causes recomputation. Focused hook-shim probe reproduced 0 initial, 0 after assets load, 1 after category change.

findings.title: Trade opportunities are hidden by an array/envelope mismatch
findings.explanation: useTrades data already equals res.trades array; AssetDetailScreen reads tradeData.trades and falls back to []. Existing trade opportunities are therefore never shown. Probe with one matching trade returned zero displayed entries.

findings.title: Hardcoded browser-local endpoints prevent ordinary remote deployment
findings.explanation: Active app calls http://localhost:4001–4007 from the browser. A deployed browser points localhost at its own computer. Gateway service exists but only unused aprenApi uses it; only unused foodAssetApi supports an environment override. No production endpoint selection is wired to active UI.

findings.title: Live records are mixed with fixture claims and empty history
findings.explanation: Kitchens, market pulse, top-pick explanations, past exchanges, contribution shares and reward history are fixed samples. Mapper forces change=0, history/log=[] and a synthetic journey. Market claims sorted by demand without sorting; detail history gets an empty polyline. This presents a product concept but does not establish provenance, pricing history, nearby demand or earned rewards from real data.

findings.title: Request failures are converted into indistinguishable empty/default states
findings.explanation: Shared active API wrapper returns null for every fetch/HTTP/parse failure. Assets map null to [], wallet maps null to missing cash/food; loading/error states are not rendered. User sees empty market/fallback balances rather than a recoverable error. This also conceals backend availability problems.

findings.title: Food-brain work in the assets service is not connected to the web experience
findings.explanation: Active asset detail requests the older intelligence service /brain/asset/:id, which uses fixed trust/liquidity and simple scoring. Rich asset profile, market intelligence, evidence and new /brain routes in assets:4003 are not called by active UI. The gateway also routes /api/brain to intelligence:4005, so it does not expose those assets routes via that prefix.

findings.title: Core card navigation is mouse-only
findings.explanation: Cards/listings/kitchens use div onClick without role/tabIndex/key handlers, so keyboard users cannot activate these navigation paths. Notification bell lacks accessible name. Search and amount inputs have placeholder/visual labels without programmatic label association.

findings.title: Food evidence and vision labels are fabricated rather than image analysis
findings.explanation: Evidence content is ignored, some scores are random and image/video reference existence increases freshness. These cannot substantiate food safety, freshness or model accuracy.

findings.title: Legacy orchestration calls an export that does not exist
findings.explanation: orchestrate awaits communication.broadcast, but module only exports communicate, so request fails with TypeError after local decision creation.

findings.title: Council expects vote fields absent from most agents
findings.explanation: Council looks for BLOCK/FAST_MOVE/PROMOTE votes, but freshness and market agents return recommendation, and trust returns REVIEW/TRUSTED. finalDecision remains MONITOR even for freshness zero.

findings.title: Agent goal is journaled but does not guide any stage
findings.explanation: goal is required and stored, while prediction/simulation/collaboration/decision receive only asset context. All goals share identical policy for the same data.

findings.title: Main agent policy recommends selling expired food
findings.explanation: freshness zero raises SELL_NOW to90, which is authorized and clears trust gate90 in autonomous SIMULATED execution. Unlike older intelligence recommendation, this path never blocks expiration. Main kernel currently simulates effects, but output is unsafe if used for commerce.

findings.title: Trust governor passes an unresolved Promise as permission
findings.explanation: getPermission is async; missing await means policy receives Promise, never matches AUTONOMOUS/ASSISTED strings for LOW risk, and return permission serializes as empty object.

findings.title: Several execution APIs report success without performing an action
findings.explanation: automation marks EXECUTED after only an allowlist check, actionExecution logs SUCCESS/POSITIVE for simulated placeholder. This is useful scaffolding but not execution completion evidence.

findings.title: Decision recommendation facade violates selector interface
findings.explanation: actionSelector expects array and returns scenario/score; facade passes data and reads action/priority/reason. Object inputs throw and array inputs yield undefined output fields.

findings.title: Forecast modules disagree on numeric versus label contracts
findings.explanation: futureState reads absent predicted_freshness/predicted_demand; predictiveIntelligence passes numbers to object APIs then treats objects as numeric forecasts. These are executable contract defects, not merely simplistic models.

findings.title: Simulation and strategy winners are predetermined by constants
findings.explanation: REDIRECT's score always exceeds SELL_NOW/WAIT for ordinary inputs; PROMOTE is always scored five above previous strategy and three above TRADE. Claims of optimized/evolved choice are unsupported by alternatives or learned outcomes.

findings.title: Predictive scenario resets expired food to full freshness
findings.explanation: data.freshness ||100 turns valid zero into100, so simulations can present expired food as fresh; demand zero similarly becomes50.

findings.title: Memory fusion expects nonexistent pattern/confidence fields
findings.explanation: patternRecognition returns patterns_found and experience_score only. Fusion persists undefined pattern/confidence and futurePrediction receives no pattern/confidence, yielding STABLE with missing confidence or SQL errors depending on constraints.

findings.title: Stored outcome existence and simulated status count as successful learning
findings.explanation: Any truthy outcome object—including {} and failure data—increases experience_score; SIMULATED status is explicitly successful positive feedback. These journals do not establish real-world predictive performance.

findings.title: Wallet funding accepts arbitrary caller amount without funding proof or idempotency
findings.explanation: Function atomically adds data.amount and records funding, but contains no amount bounds, payment verification or idempotency. Caller-level protections must be verified separately; transaction and wallet lock alone do not prevent arbitrary or repeated credits.

findings.title: Permission routes serialize unresolved promises
findings.explanation: Both POST setPermission and GET getPermission are async but not awaited. JSON permission becomes {}; async rejection bypasses local try/catch in POST and no error handling in GET.

findings.title: Caller context can replace persisted food condition scores
findings.explanation: Freshness/demand/value prefer inputData and final ...inputData can overwrite even normalized/trust fields. This supports simulations but is not authoritative food safety evidence for future real execution. Kernel effects are currently explicitly SIMULATED.

findings.title: Installers are unsafe to treat as a repeatable setup sequence
findings.explanation: Early upgrade-food-assets overwrites the entire db.js and server.js, discarding later integration. repair-assets-server removes everything from freshness route to app.listen. Restart helpers kill any port4003 process or every matching node src/server.js. Many scripts cd ~/apren, so running them from this clone still modifies a different checkout or fails. These are historical patch artifacts with order/location assumptions, not a migration runner.

findings.title: Shared schema definitions conflict and SQL errors do not reliably stop the scripts
findings.explanation: Different layers define identical table names with incompatible shapes/types, e.g. predictions.prediction TEXT vs JSONB and strategies.strategy TEXT vs JSONB. CREATE/ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS never changes the existing type, so outcome depends on installation order. SQL invocations lack psql ON_ERROR_STOP; shell set -e alone does not make each SQL statement failure terminate a psql session. No canonical schema/versioned migration source is provided by these scripts.

findings.title: Generated modules overwrite interfaces still used by earlier live handlers
findings.explanation: Historical route generators leave direct routes in server.js while later generators overwrite imported module APIs. Examples currently called are decisionEngine.evaluateAsset, foodBrainOrchestrator.history and feedbackEngine.recordFeedback, but latest generated modules expose decide(data), orchestrate only, and record/history respectively. Require/syntax checks pass because they do not exercise those properties.

findings.title: Persistent permission migration misses await at its callers
findings.explanation: permissionMemoryEngine becomes asynchronous, but governor and permission routes still use returned promises as values. Installer attempts exact text replacement with an extra space before data.userId, which does not match checked-in governor. Policy compares Promise to AUTONOMOUS and fails; JSON responses serialize Promise as an empty object and async rejections are not caught by synchronous try/catch.

findings.title: Earlier council loses food-safety votes after agent replacement
findings.explanation: Council checks agent results.vote for BLOCK/FAST_MOVE/PROMOTE. Layer37 overwrites freshnessAgent and marketAgent to return signal/recommendation instead. Current council no longer sees their expiry-block or promotion votes and falls back to MONITOR, though numerical confidences still look plausible.

findings.title: One DB installer does not forward its SQL heredoc to the container
findings.explanation: docker exec apren-postgres psql is fed a host heredoc without docker exec -i. Unlike other scripts using -i, it does not keep container stdin open, so intended lifecycle/transaction DDL is not reliably applied even if command completes.

findings.title: A historical evidence repair writes standalone SQL into JavaScript
findings.explanation: fix-evidence-table-sync inserts raw CREATE TABLE text directly before module.exports in src/db.js without db.exec/template literal wrapper. The existence of a later regex repair explains a historical syntax failure and is another reason not to rerun patch scripts blindly.

findings.title: Many named intelligence/execution layers are fixed heuristics or status placeholders
findings.explanation: Examples include random evidence verification, four constant negotiation arguments, SIMULATED_EXECUTION recorded SUCCESS, and higher freshness simply for providing media-reference strings. These demonstrate plumbing and persistence, not validated computer vision, learned prediction, genuine negotiation or completed external action. Many corresponding generated files are still identical to current code.
